subject: Data scope redlines and runtime-access request — routing for Product/Security sign-off
messages:
From: Samir Rao <samir@horizonhealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Horizon Health Procurement <procurement@horizonhealth.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Redlines: Data scope & runtime access

Hi Ben —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement asked me to send our proposed DPA redlines specific to runtime access and data use. The key ask is that we be granted the ability to access runtime-derived session metadata for analytics (session IDs, anonymized token counts, and error-rate metrics) and to retain those derived records for a 12-month analytics window. We are NOT requesting model training rights, simply telemetry and aggregated usage stats.

Attached is the proposed redline (horizon-proposed-dpa-redline.docx) — Section 3.2 adds a clause: "Customer may access runtime-derived session metadata for the purpose of service analytics and billing reconciliation; such data shall be pseudonymized and used solely for aggregate analytics and troubleshooting and shall not be used to train models."

Can Redwood confirm (1) that runtime access in Hosted mode will not expose prompt/response contents, (2) what controls exist for pseudonymization, and (3) retention options? Procurement needs a response by end of week to keep the contracting timeline.

Regards,
Samir Rao
Senior Procurement Manager
Horizon Health

[Attachment: horizon-proposed-dpa-redline.docx (DOCX)]

Samir —

Thanks for sending this over and for the clear ask. Looping in our Legal (Olga), Security (Rishi) and Product (Laura) to validate the proposed language and confirm the runtime guarantees. We understand procurement has an aggressive timeline; we’ll aim to get a consolidated answer by Friday EOD PT.

Quick note for clarity: When you reference "runtime-derived session metadata" can you confirm you mean non-content telemetry (session IDs, anonymized token/latency metrics, error codes) and not actual prompt/response text? I want to ensure we all call out the same thing in the DPA.

Ben
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Redlines: Data scope & runtime access — need Product/Sec confirmation

Team — forwarding Horizon’s redline. I’ve read the draft and have three legal points that depend on Product/Security input before I can sign off:

1) Definition scope: we need to agree on a clear definition for "runtime-derived session metadata" that explicitly excludes prompt/response content and PII.
2) Pseudonymization guarantees: what controls are in place to ensure identifiers are not reversible; if we can’t guarantee it, we should limit retention or add additional access controls.
3) Auditability: Procurement wants a 12-month retention for analytics; Security should confirm whether we can provide logs/evidence for SOC2 reviewers without exposing sensitive content.

Please comment inline on the attached and propose exact language for legal to insert. If Product and Security give a thumbs-up on the protections and language below, Legal will accept the redline with a standard non-training carveout.

Suggested next steps: Product to propose an explicit sentence we can paste, Security to confirm pseudonymization and logging approach, then Legal will prepare a counter-redline.

Thanks — Olga
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

[Attachment: horizon-proposed-dpa-redline.docx (DOCX)]

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 15:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Redlines: Data scope & runtime access — technical clarifications

Quick technical notes from Security:

- Confirmed: Hosted runtime does not expose prompt/response text via the analytics endpoints we expose. The runtime emits metrics and aggregated counters only. We do persist ephemeral KV caches for performance, but they are not surfaced and are encrypted at rest.

- Pseudonymization: We can provide hashed session IDs (SHA256 with per-customer salt) so identifiers are non-reversible by default. However, if a customer supplies their own session identifiers that map back to PII, they remain responsible for that mapping.

- Retention & audit: We can implement a 12-month retention window for the derived telemetry and provide audit exports (CSV summary of aggregated metrics) for SOC2 review. We will redact any fields that could contain content snippets. For documented evidence we typically provide: retention configuration screenshot, example export (audit-evidence-sample.pdf), and runtime-access-diagram.png showing non-content telemetry flow.

- One ask: add an explicit non-training clause in the DPA (if not already present) and a line that prohibits re-identification attempts. Also recommend logging access control (role-based) for any exports containing session IDs.

If Legal drafts language accepting hashed session IDs + no-training + role-based export controls, Security can approve operationally.

—Rishi
Head of Security Engineering, Redwood Inference

[Attachment: audit-evidence-sample.pdf (PDF)]

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Samir Rao <samir@horizonhealth.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 16:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Redlines: Data scope & runtime access — proposed Product wording

Samir / Team —

Thanks for the clear ask and the draft. To avoid ambiguity I propose the following single-sentence addition we can paste into Section 3.2: 

"Customer may access pseudonymized runtime-derived telemetry (e.g., hashed session identifiers, anonymized token counts, latency metrics, and aggregated error codes) solely for service analytics and billing reconciliation. Such telemetry will not include prompt or response content, will be pseudonymized using customer-scoped salts, and will not be used to train any models. Access to exports containing pseudonymized identifiers will be restricted via role-based controls and logged for audit."

Operational notes: we can implement hashed session IDs with per-customer salt (as Rishi suggested) and enable a 12-month configurable retention on the analytics index. We will prepare the export artifact and a configuration screenshot for Legal/SOC reviewers.

If Security is comfortable with the role-based export logging language and Legal is happy with the sentence, Ben please circulate our counter-redline to Samir and procurement and indicate expected timeline (we can ship the counter today and target signature next week).

Laura Bennett
VP Product, Redwood Inference
